free_tier.stated: a free certificate on every zone, covering the apex and one level of subdomain

per_object_cap.stated: covers example.com and app.example.com, not a.b.example.com; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager

retention.stated: the certificate is issued and renewed by Cloudflare while the zone is active

interface_detail: automatic on a proxied zone; no client API of its own, and the zone API reports the certificate
tooling: nothing to run: the certificate appears on the zone
chaining: the certificate half of the free endpoint, from the same account and zone as the DNS and the tunnel

limits.value: one level of subdomain only; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account and a zone on Cloudflare nameservers

confidence_note: the one-level coverage limit is stated across Cloudflare's TLS documentation and repeated in third-party summaries; the product page was reached only as a stub, so this is reported.

evidence.proved: Universal SSL is free on every plan; the one-level subdomain coverage limit and the Advanced Certificate Manager upgrade path are the substance

notes: The one-level limit is the trap. A per-tenant scheme at tenant.app.example.com needs a paid certificate manager, or a wildcard from Let's Encrypt over DNS-01, which is free.
